summary.headline: Sumeet Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35.23% YoY to INR 364 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to 2.53% as spread over material cost narrowed to 17.1%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR 364 crore in Q2 FY27, up 35.23% YoY and 33.71% QoQ, with H1 revenue at about INR 636 crore versus INR 517 crore a year earlier. EBITDA including other income fell to INR 9.22 crore from about INR 14 crore, with margin down to 2.53% from 5.79%, which management attributed to a narrower spread over material cost (17.1% vs 23%) as volumes were scaled. Finance cost fell about 25% and PAT was INR 4.40 crore versus INR 9.86 crore a year ago. The balance sheet strengthened after the rights issue, with net worth near INR 417 crore, borrowings at INR 137 crore and cash at INR 160 crore.

segments.name: Yarn / FDY (fully drawn/textured yarn)
segments.commentary: Capacity raised by 40 TPD from 120 to 160 TPD; management says new production will go to value added yarns (dope dyed bright, ketonic, BSY). Management expects FDY and PET chips to drive the 30%+ revenue growth targeted for FY27.

segments.name: PET chips (bottle grade)
segments.commentary: Nakoda subsidiary Sumi Speciality Chips is building a 1.4 lakh tpa bottle-grade PET chips plant in Surat, expected operational by Q2 FY28, adding about INR 200 crore turnover and INR 70 crore EBITDA (about 5-6% margin).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR 1,300 crore, based on current capacity and the 40 TPD expansion; management says the company is on track.
EBITDA margin expected to recover to about 5-6% within the next two quarters, helped by lower crude and raw material prices and wedding-season demand.
12 MW solar plant to be commissioned by December 2026, taking renewables to about 50-55% of consumption; expected to add INR 23-25 crore of benefit from power-cost savings, first benefit in Q4 FY27.
Nakoda phase 3 plant expected to start commercial operation by Q2 FY28 and generate about INR 1,200 crore annual revenue once fully operational.
H2 FY27 depreciation guided at about INR 5 crore per quarter (about INR 9.22 crore for the half).
capex_capacity: Plant running at 95-98% utilisation; 40 TPD added, taking capacity from 120 to 160 TPD.

Rights issue completed in Q1 FY27 with net proceeds of INR 194.9 crore: INR 100 crore working capital, INR 85.9 crore Nakoda asset integration, INR 9 crore debt repayment (earlier plan had about INR 22 crore for solar and INR 23 crore debt reduction, reallocated).
12 MW solar plant costing about INR 40 crore, funded from a pre-rights-issue term loan; management says no additional debt raised.
Plans to move up to 50% of capacity into value added yarn and add texturising machines to convert POY to DTY (forward integration under study).
Nakoda 450 TPD CP capacity being started to support bottle-grade chips; Nakoda expansion of 400 TPD referenced.
demand_pricing: Receivables rose about 42% from INR 133 crore (March 2026) to INR 189 crore (September 2026); management attributed this to stopping cash discounts to agents and customers now that working capital is healthy, plus higher finished-goods prices after raw material inflation.
Management says receivables remain in line with industry standards; prices lag raw material costs, compressing margins.

Bottle-grade PET chips: about 50% of domestic demand still imported from China; management cites a supply shortfall and an untapped export market. Management put its 400 TPD share at about 10% of a roughly 4,000 TPD market; a competitor-cited concern about PET chip overcapacity was raised on the call.
Q1 FY27 sales volume about 23,000 tons vs Q2 FY27 about 29,000 tons (all products combined, including chips).

qa_highlights.question: Volumes sold in Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave about 23,000 tons in Q1 and about 29,000 tons in Q2 FY27, all products combined. A split across PET chips, FDY, POY and PDY was promised for future presentations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash discounts given during tight finances were stopped, and raw material-driven price increases and weak market liquidity also contributed; it stated receivables are within industry norms.

qa_highlights.question: Cost and funding of the 12/16 MW solar project and the reallocation of IPO/rights funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 12 MW plant costs about INR 40 crore, funded from a pre-rights-issue term loan, with capex funds reshuffled from debt repayment to expansion; no new debt raised.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to return to about 5-6% within two quarters as raw material prices fall and demand improves after the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bottle-grade PET chips market oversupplied?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bottle-grade chips face a shortage, with about 50% imported, and that the 400 TPD addition is about 10% of a roughly 4,000 TPD market; the overcapacity concern applies to other PET chip grades.

qa_highlights.question: H2 FY27 depreciation and H1 power cost?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 depreciation guided at about INR 5 crore per quarter; H1 FY27 power cost was about INR 39 crore excluding fuel. The FY26 power cost figure was not available on the call.

risks_watch: Gross spread over material cost fell to 17.1% from 23%; margin recovery to 5-6% depends on crude and raw material prices staying lower.
Receivables up about 42% to INR 189 crore; collection trend and credit terms to be tracked next quarter.
Execution risk on Nakoda phase 3 PET chips (Q2 FY28 start) and the December 2026 solar commissioning.
Management did not provide the FY26 power cost or the FY26 volume split; several questions were deferred to offline follow-up.
Some answers were inconsistent (e.g., margin and revenue figures were partly misstated during the call), so the figures should be checked against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and on the 1,300 crore revenue target and margin recovery, but the answers on receivables, funding reallocation and the PET chips market were defensive and sometimes unclear. Management often deferred specific numbers to later presentations or offline discussions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin back to 5-6% from 2.53% in Q2 FY27, citing lower crude and raw material prices and wedding-season demand; the 12 MW solar plant adds INR 23-25 crore of power savings with first benefit in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 40 TPD yarn addition is already commissioned (120 to 160 TPD), the 12 MW solar plant is due by December 2026, and the 1.4 lakh tpa Surat PET chips plant is due by Q2 FY28, adding about INR 200 crore turnover.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Sales volume rose from about 23,000 tons in Q1 FY27 to about 29,000 tons in Q2 FY27 with 95-98% utilisation and the 160 TPD capacity now live, and management targets FY27 revenue of about INR 1,300 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 95-98% and the company is weighing up to 50% of capacity moving into value-added yarn plus texturising machines (forward integration under study), with the Nakoda phase 3 plant already in progress.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the FY27 revenue target of about INR 1,300 crore and the 5-6% margin rather than raising them, and the FY27 revenue figure was referenced by an analyst rather than confirmed by management.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin was 2.53% in Q2 against a 5-6% target, the spread over material cost fell to 17.1% from 23%, and receivables rose 42% to INR 189 crore, so the margin recovery depends on raw material prices staying lower.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New production from the 40 TPD addition is going to value-added yarns (dope dyed bright, ketonic, BSY), and texturising machines to convert POY to DTY are under study.

rows.label: Bottle-grade PET chips import substitution
rows.why: About 50% of domestic bottle-grade demand is still imported from China, and the 400 TPD Nakoda share is about 10% of a roughly 4,000 TPD market, but the Surat plant only starts by Q2 FY28 and a PET overcapacity concern was raised.

rows.label: Receivables normalisation
rows.why: Receivables rose about 42% from INR 133 crore to INR 189 crore after cash discounts were stopped, and management says this is within industry norms but collections will be tracked next quarter.

rows.label: Gearing reduction
rows.why: Gearing fell to 0.33x from 0.75x after the rights issue, with net worth near INR 417 crore against borrowings of INR 137 crore and cash of INR 160 crore.
